stimulus.text: And it hath accordingly happened that an open resistance to the execution of the laws hath actually taken place in the town of Boston, and the neighbourhood thereof... so much of the charter, granted by their majesties King William and Queen Mary to the inhabitants of the said province of the Massachusetts Bay, in New England... be revoked... and that the council, or court of assistants... shall be composed of such of the inhabitants... as shall be thereunto nominated and appointed by his Majesty...

source: original; stimulus viewed before writing — Massachusetts Government Act, 1774 (abridged), public domain.

books.section: A. Colonial Resistance to British Policies in the Aftermath of the French and Indian War
The Sugar Act, the Currency Act, and the Stamp Act

stem: Which of the following was one of the Coercive Acts of 1774?

options.misconception: The Sugar Act was 1764, ten years earlier — a revenue measure, not one of the 1774 punishments for the Tea Party.
The Stamp Act was 1765 and was repealed in 1766 — it cannot be one of the 1774 Coercive Acts.
The Townshend Acts were 1767, and their duties were mostly repealed in 1770 — they predate the Coercive Acts by seven years.

rationales.D: The Boston Port Act closed Boston's port until the destroyed tea was paid for. It was one of the four Coercive Acts of 1774, passed to punish Massachusetts for the Tea Party.
rationales.A: The Sugar Act belongs to 1764. It was a revenue law, a decade before the Coercive Acts.
rationales.B: The Stamp Act belongs to 1765, and it was repealed in 1766. It cannot be a 1774 act.
rationales.C: The Townshend Acts belong to 1767. Their duties were mostly repealed in 1770.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what year the acts belong to. The Coercive Acts were 1774, passed after the Boston Tea Party of December 1773.
2. Test each option by date. The Sugar Act was 1764, the Stamp Act 1765, the Townshend Acts 1767 — all too early.
3. Keep the one that fits. The Boston Port Act closed the port until the tea was paid for — a 1774 punishment for a 1773 act.
Remember: dates are the fastest filter — when options span a decade, sort them by year first.
